subject.title: [Bug]: `openclaw models auth login` on node host writes OAuth token locally instead of syncing to gateway

question: Should `openclaw models auth login` on a node host connected to a non-loopback gateway fail closed before provider auth starts, or should OpenClaw add a gateway-owned credential forwarding/sync path?
rationale: Both valid repairs decide where OAuth credentials are minted and stored across hosts, so automation should not choose the cross-host credential policy without maintainer intent.

options.title: Fail Closed On Remote Node Hosts
options.body: Block login before OAuth/token creation when `node.json` points at a non-loopback gateway and tell the operator to run auth on the gateway host.

options.title: Design Gateway Credential Sync
options.body: Keep node-host login convenience by adding an explicit gateway API for credential transfer with security review and upgrade tests.

options.title: Document Node-Local Auth Only
options.body: Accept the current ownership boundary by documenting that node-host auth login only affects the node-local store and requiring gateway-host authentication.

recommendation.title: Fail Closed On Remote Node Hosts
recommendation.body: Block login before OAuth/token creation when `node.json` points at a non-loopback gateway and tell the operator to run auth on the gateway host.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent has both recent remote-node OAuth guard history and the clearest linked maintainer follow-up on this exact issue.
